ops.title: Operations overview
ops.noAirlineHint: Found your own airline: choose a name, colours, a home airport and your starting capital.
ops.notInstalled: Not yet: use “Add to Home Screen” / “Install”

modeHint.realtime: Time runs continuously. Pause any time; choose a speed from 1 game minute to 1 game day per second.
modeHint.weekly: Time stands still while you decide. “End week” simulates the next 7 days in one go.
modeHint.realclock: The game runs on the real clock: VIE–JFK takes about 9 real hours. The world keeps going while the app is closed; when you come back, the missed time is simulated and summed up for you.

settings.title: Settings
settings.dataNote: Built with open data. All sources are listed in the project's DATA_SOURCES file.
settings.autosaveNote: The game saves itself automatically on this device, in its own save slot. Copies, other games, export and import: Saves.
settings.realClockHint: Switch this game to the real clock: from now on 1 game minute = 1 real minute, and the world keeps running while the app is closed. The game is at {{date}}: if that is before today, the time until today is simulated first; if it is later, the game keeps its date and runs on at real speed.
settings.realClockConfirm: Switch to the real clock? Pause and speed buttons disappear, and the world keeps running while the app is closed. This can't be undone.

airport.marketNote: Catchment = people living in cities within 100 km. Passenger demand is calculated from these figures in Phase 1.4.

sim.liveHint: Real clock: 1 game minute = 1 real minute

newGame.scenarioStartupHint: Your own airline: name, colours, hub and money – today or in any year since 1970.
newGame.takeoverHint: Become CEO of the real airline – today or in any year since 1970: its aircraft, routes and timetable of that year, with its partners of the time.
newGame.takeoverNotes: Routes and flights per week come from Wikipedia and Eurostat (summer 2024, scaled to the season); the game plans the timetable on the real fleet (real timetables may not be copied, so it is “modelled”). Build years, which aircraft are leased and the cash are modelled too, because the airline doesn’t publish them. The Embraer 195s leave by 2028; 17 new A320neo-family aircraft arrive from the group. Summer-only holiday routes rest in the winter. Your partners never attack your routes, and some of their passengers connect onto your flights in Vienna.
newGame.takeoverScheduling: Detailed: the game plans every aircraft’s rotations on the real fleet; you can change any flight.
newGame.title: New game
newGame.intro: Found a startup – in 2026 or any year since 1970 – or take over a real airline. Choose your scenario below.
newGame.name: Airline name
newGame.codesHint: The 2-character code goes in front of flight numbers (like OS 51), the 3-letter ICAO code is used by air traffic control.
newGame.hubHint: Your books are kept in {{currency}}. Aircraft leases are priced in US dollars, as in the real industry.

capitalHint.tight: Like a very small startup: one or two aircraft, every mistake hurts.
capitalHint.standard: Roughly what real low-cost startups raised: a small fleet to start.
capitalHint.funded: A startup with strong investors behind it: room for wide-bodies.

newGame.laterHint: Hardcore realism and real airlines of past years arrive in later steps.
newGame.replaceWarning: You already have a game running. It stays in Saves.

eraHint.1970: Jumbo jets arrive, flying is a luxury, IATA fixes the fares.
eraHint.1980: Oil crisis, sky-high fuel; US airlines just deregulated.
eraHint.1990: The Iron Curtain is gone, Europe still regulated, the Gulf War looms.
eraHint.2000: Low-cost airlines rise, the euro is coming – then 9/11.
eraHint.2010: Ash cloud, debt crisis, low-cost carriers everywhere.

newGame.todayHint: Today's world: real airlines with their networks, today's prices.
newGame.historicalHint: A historical game: airports, aircraft types, fuel prices, exchange rates and real events of that time. Your books are kept in the money of the time (e.g. schilling until 1999), prices and fares are those of the year. Your rivals are the real airlines of that year – including ones that have closed since – with the aircraft types they flew and modelled routes; they start and stop flying on their real dates. Before deregulation fares are fixed by the IATA tariff. The real clock is only available for today.
newGame.hubNotYet: This airport didn't exist yet in {{year}}. Please choose another home airport.
newGame.takeoverNotesPast: Austrian in {{year}}: the fleet of that year from Wikipedia (types and years; numbers of aircraft partly modelled), registrations made up in Austrian's real OE-L series (old registers aren't open data), all aircraft owned. Routes are modelled like those of the other airlines of the year, the timetable is planned by the game, the cash is modelled from the size of the fleet. Partners follow history: its subsidiaries Tyrolean (from 1997) and Lauda Air (from 2001) – their aircraft and Vienna routes become yours –, Qualiflyer with Swissair (1998–2000), Star Alliance (from 2000) and the Lufthansa Group (from September 2009). Nothing is planned for you: new aircraft you order yourself.

fleet.title: Fleet
fleet.noGame: Found an airline first, then you can lease aircraft here.
fleet.empty: You have no aircraft yet. Lessors are offering used aircraft on the lease market.
fleet.marketIntro: Used aircraft offered by leasing companies. You pay a security deposit now; monthly rent starts on delivery. New offers appear at the start of each month, old ones expire.
fleet.leased: Lease signed! Your {{type}} will be registered as {{registration}}.
fleet.runwayWarning: Fully loaded, this type needs {{needed}} m of runway; {{hub}} has {{runway}} m. It can still fly shorter routes with less fuel.
fleet.confirmText_one: Pay a deposit of {{deposit}} now. Rent of {{rent}} per month starts on delivery ({{date}}) and runs for {{count}} year.
fleet.confirmText_other: Pay a deposit of {{deposit}} now. Rent of {{rent}} per month starts on delivery ({{date}}) and runs for {{count}} years.
fleet.paymentPlan: Payments: {{now}} now, {{before}} in the two years before delivery, {{delivery}} on delivery.
fleet.orderCabin: Cabin ({{seats}} seats, can be changed before delivery)

ask.return_one: Return this aircraft to the lessor now? The lessor charges {{fee}} (60 % of the rent still owed) and pays back the deposit of {{deposit}}. Its flights on {{count}} route are cancelled.
ask.return_other: Return this aircraft to the lessor now? The lessor charges {{fee}} (60 % of the rent still owed) and pays back the deposit of {{deposit}}. Its flights on {{count}} routes are cancelled.
ask.extend: New rent {{rent}} per month (today's market rate for an aircraft of this age), lease until {{until}}.
ask.sell_one: Sell for about {{price}} (market value minus 3 % broker's fee)? Its flights on {{count}} route are cancelled.
ask.sell_other: Sell for about {{price}} (market value minus 3 % broker's fee)? Its flights on {{count}} routes are cancelled.
ask.scrap_one: Scrap it? A scrapyard pays {{price}} for engines and parts. Its flights on {{count}} route are cancelled.
ask.scrap_other: Scrap it? A scrapyard pays {{price}} for engines and parts. Its flights on {{count}} routes are cancelled.
ask.cancel: Cancel the order? The {{lost}} already paid is lost (deposits are not refunded).
ask.buy: Buy for {{price}}, paid now? It arrives on {{date}} after inspection, paperwork and repaint.
ask.order_one: Order {{count}} {{type}} for {{total}}? {{now}} deposit now, the first aircraft arrives on {{first}}.
ask.order_other: Order {{count}} {{type}} for {{total}}? {{now}} deposit now, the first aircraft arrives on {{first}}.

fleet.buyIntro: Used aircraft for sale by lessors and traders, priced around their market value. You pay the full price now; the aircraft is yours, so there is no rent, but it is written off in your accounts over its remaining life.
fleet.orderIntro: New aircraft from the manufacturers. The order books are full: popular jets ordered today arrive years from now. You pay a 1 % deposit now, pre-delivery payments (30 %) in the two years before delivery and the rest on delivery. Prices are typical prices after discounts (about half the list price); bigger orders get a bit more off.

block.chinaOnly: only for Chinese airlines so far
block.eastBloc: Soviet type: not for sale to Western airlines before 1992

fleet.orderNote: Backlog years and prices are modelled from public news reports (manufacturers' order files may not be reused). Leasing (also new aircraft from lessors) and buying used are the quick ways to grow.

network.title: Network
network.intro: Your routes from the hub. Simple scheduling: you choose aircraft and round trips per week, the game sets the departure times.
network.empty: No routes yet. Open your first route to start flying.
network.maxFrequency_one: This aircraft has room for {{count}} more round trip.
network.maxFrequency_other: This aircraft has room for up to {{count}} round trips.
network.noCompetition: no airline flies this route non-stop
network.fixedNote: Not included: crew salaries and lease for {{registration}} ({{cost}} per week), which all routes of this aircraft share, and the airline's overheads. The route uses {{hours}} block hours per week.
network.forecastNote: Forecast for this month's season once the route is known; new routes start with about 60 % of these passengers and grow over 8 weeks. Summer is busier than winter, and fuel prices change every week. Other airlines react to your prices and timetable within about a month.
network.closeConfirm: Close this route? Flights stop immediately.
network.plusConnections: Plus one-stop connections via other hubs. Passengers changing between your own flights at your hub are counted separately (they pay a share of their whole journey's fare).
network.introDetailed: Your routes from the hub with your own timetable: every flight has a departure time, days of operation and an aircraft.
network.fixedNoteDetailed: Not included: crew salaries and leases of {{registration}} ({{cost}} per week together), which they share with their other routes, and the airline's overheads. The route uses {{hours}} block hours per week.
network.regulatedFares: Regulated route: until {{date}} governments and the IATA tariff fix the fares here, so you can only charge ±10 % around the official fare. No price wars.

finance.title: Finance
finance.cashNote: Ticket revenue and flight costs are booked every day; lease rents leave on the 1st of each month.
finance.pnlNote: Lease costs are spread over the days of the month here, even though the cash leaves once a month. Overheads are paid from the day the airline is founded, even without aircraft.
finance.directNote: Route result = ticket revenue minus fuel, maintenance, fees, handling and sales. Crews and leases are paid per aircraft, not per route.
finance.chartHint: Green = profit, red = loss, light = period still running. Tap a bar to see that period in detail; swipe sideways for older periods. Weeks are kept for two years, months for the whole game.

airlines.title: Airlines
airlines.intro: The real airlines of the world ({{count}} with a known network). Biggest first; search by name, code or hub.
airlines.search: Search airline, code or hub (e.g. OS, Ryanair, VIE)

colorSource.generated: generated colours (real colours not yet entered)

airlines.networkNote: Routes from Wikipedia's airport articles. Weekly flights: official Eurostat totals (season {{season}}); where several airlines share a route, the total is split between them (an estimate, marked “modelled”), and routes without official numbers are filled in by the game's demand model.
airlines.closedRoutes_one: {{count}} route given up in this game.
airlines.closedRoutes_other: {{count}} routes given up in this game.
airlines.playerRuns: You run this airline: its network and fleet in your game are yours (Network and Fleet screens). Below is the real-world data it started from.
airlines.modelledNote: Modelled for your historical game: the routes of today's airlines from this country, only where the economy of the year could fill them.

eraFleet.wikipedia: Types it flew in {{year}}: from the airline's fleet tables on Wikipedia. Numbers of aircraft are estimates.
eraFleet.today: Types it flew in {{year}}: today's fleet where the type already existed (Wikipedia has no historical fleet table for it). Numbers are estimates.
eraFleet.typical: Wikipedia has no fleet table for this airline: it flies the typical aircraft of its time.

airlines.eraNetworkNote: Routes modelled for {{year}}: an airline flying today keeps the part of today's network that the economy of the time could fill and that it had grown to; airlines that have closed since fly from their real hubs to the destinations the demand model ranks best. Weekly flights follow the demand of the time.
airlines.introEra: Your game is in {{year}}: these {{count}} airlines were flying then — today's airlines that already existed and airlines that have closed since (Pan Am, Swissair, Interflug …), with their real hubs, the aircraft types they flew and their real colours where known. Their routes are modelled. Airlines start and stop flying on their real dates. Countries without a real airline in the data have a modelled national carrier.
airlines.fictionalNote: A fictional airline founded in your game on {{date}}: made-up name, code and colours. It flies the typical aircraft of its time and grows, shrinks or fails like a real startup.

sources.title: Data sources
sources.intro: This game is built on open data. Thank you to everyone who collects and shares it. Real airlines appear with their names and colours, never with their logos.
sources.notes: Wikipedia-based data in this game is published under CC BY-SA 4.0 (share-alike). Full list with download dates and how each dataset is processed: docs/DATA_SOURCES.md in the game's GitHub repository.

tagHint.official: From official statistics or registers (e.g. Eurostat, FAA).
tagHint.hand-checked: Checked by hand against the airline's own information.
tagHint.modelled: Estimated by the game's demand model where no real number is available.

use.ourairports: All airports with scheduled flights: position, runways, size. Also the closed airports of historical games (Kai Tak, Munich-Riem, Berlin Tegel, Tempelhof, Schönefeld, Athens Ellinikon, Oslo Fornebu, Denver Stapleton …).
use.geonames: City populations (catchment and market size) and time zones.
use.worldbank: Wealth (GDP per person) and tourism per country. Since Phase 5.2 also population, GDP per person, exchange rates and air passengers carried since 1960, for demand in the past.
use.naturalearth: Coastlines and borders of the map.
use.openfreemap: Fonts for the airport codes on the map.
use.wikipedia: Which airline flies where (airport articles), airline business models, hubs, bases, fleets and seat layouts (airline articles), and which aircraft types each airline flew in which years (historical fleet tables). The real event timeline since 1970 links each event to the article its facts come from.
use.wikidata: Airline names, codes, countries, alliances and parent companies; links between articles and airports. Opening dates of airports (which airports existed in a historical year). Airlines that have closed since 1970 with their founding and closing days, hubs and successors.
use.eurostat: Real passenger numbers, seats and flights per route in Europe (summer 2024), used for demand and for the airlines' weekly flights.
use.eia: The real jet fuel price, week by week in 2026. Monthly history since 1974 (estimated from crude oil before mid-1975).
use.faa: Individual aircraft (registration, type, year) of US airlines.
use.austrocontrol: Individual aircraft of Austrian airlines, including the operator.
use.iaa: Individual aircraft of Irish airlines (Ryanair, Aer Lingus).
use.reports: Published totals (passengers, load factor, revenue, margin, transfer passengers at Vienna) used only to check that the real airlines in the game earn and fill their planes about as they really do.
use.manufacturers: Aircraft performance: seats, range, take-off distance, weight.
use.bls: US consumer prices since 1913, to show historical aircraft prices in the money of any year.
use.fed: Daily exchange rates since 1971 (incl. the Austrian schilling and the other old euro currencies), for the History screen and historical start years.

timetable.title: Timetable

mode.simple: Simple scheduling: the game sets the times.

modeHint.simple: You choose round trips per week; the game plans departure times (from 06:00 hub time). You can switch to Detailed later.
modeHint.detailed: You set every flight yourself: departure time, days of operation, aircraft and ground time — like a real airline's network planning.

timetable.switchConfirm: Switch to detailed scheduling? Your current flights become a timetable you can edit. This cannot be undone.
timetable.hint: Times are local: departure in {{hub}} time, the return in {{dest}} time. The ground time includes unloading, cleaning, catering and boarding (at least the aircraft's minimum turnaround); 8 hours or more is a night stop.
timetable.boardNote: Local times at each airport. Days: 1 = Monday … 7 = Sunday, as in airline timetables; +1 = arrives the next day.
timetable.timesNote: Passengers choose by departure time: business travellers want early mornings out and evenings back, holidaymakers are flexible but avoid night flights; Fridays and Sundays are busier than Tuesdays. Flights close to a competitor's (or your own) share their passengers. Eastbound flights are faster (westerly winds). Competitors' times are generated by the game (real times may not be copied), marked “modelled”; * = not every day.

timeline.title: Week of {{registration}} (hub time)
timeline.label: Rotation chart of {{registration}}
timeline.note: Each row is a day in hub local time: flight out, time at the destination (light), flight back, turnaround (faint). Magenta = the route you are editing, red = collision.

saves.title: Saves
saves.intro: Every game has its own save slot on this device and saves itself automatically. Keep copies to go back to, and export files as a backup or to continue on another device.
saves.autosave: Saved automatically: when you pause, change something, leave the app, and every 15 seconds while the clock runs.
saves.restoreConfirm: Go back to “{{name}}”? The game continues from this copy; progress made since then is lost unless you save a copy of it first.
saves.deleteGameConfirm_one: Delete the game “{{name}}” and its copy from this device? Exported files are not affected.
saves.deleteGameConfirm_other: Delete the game “{{name}}” and its {{count}} copies from this device? Exported files are not affected.
saves.importFailed: This file is not a save from this game (or it is damaged).
saves.loadFailed: This save could not be opened.
saves.failed: Something went wrong while saving or reading.
saves.exportNote: Export creates a small compressed “.amsave” file. To continue on another device, send it there (e.g. by e-mail or cloud drive) and use “Import file”. With cloud sync (above) this happens by itself.
saves.storage: Storage used by the game: {{used}} MB of about {{quota}} MB.
saves.persisted: The browser keeps these saves permanently.
saves.notPersisted: The browser may delete them if space runs low: export a backup now and then (installing the app helps).

dashboard.title: Key figures
dashboard.period: Last full week, from {{week}}; ▲▼ = change against the week before, line = last 12 weeks (point at it for values).
dashboard.waiting: The key figures appear after your first full week of flying (weeks run Monday to Sunday).

hint.cash: Money in the bank. Below zero, the airline is in trouble.
hint.result: Revenue minus all costs (incl. crews, leases, overheads) in the last full week.
hint.margin: Result as a share of revenue. Good European airlines make 5–15 % over a year.
hint.loadFactor: Share of seat-km sold (RPK ÷ ASK). European airlines: about 80–90 %.
hint.rask: Revenue per available seat-km: what each seat flown one km earns.
hint.cask: Cost per available seat-km (all costs). Earns money when RASK is higher.
hint.caskExFuel: CASK without fuel: the costs the airline controls itself.
hint.yield: Revenue per passenger-km: the average price per km flown.
hint.utilisation: Block hours per aircraft per day. Short-haul airlines: about 9–12 h.

dashboard.note: Route results here are before crews, leases and overheads. Utilisation uses today's number of aircraft.

cabin.summary: {{seats}} seats of {{max}} allowed by the exits · {{used}} % of the cabin length used
cabin.expected: Passengers expect about {{score}} in this class
cabin.comfortNote: Rating of the seat on short and long flights (0–100). Green: as good as passengers expect of this class, amber: a bit worse, red: much worse. Pitch = distance from one seat to the same point of the seat in front. European business has a movable curtain: on each flight, rows business doesn't need are sold as economy.
cabin.freeBeforeDelivery: Free: the aircraft isn't delivered yet, the lessor fits the new cabin during the transition.
cabin.quote: Refit: {{cost}}, {{days}} days in the hangar ({{seats}} new seats). Paid now, written off over 6 years. The aircraft's flights are cancelled during the refit.

reputation.title: Reputation
reputation.scoreHint: What passengers say about you (0–100, 60 = as expected). Built slowly, week by week, from every passenger's trip. For comparison, real airlines in the game: network carriers {{legacy}}, low-cost {{lowcost}} (modelled).
reputation.awarenessHint: How well known you are in your markets. It grows with the passengers you carry; unknown airlines win fewer travellers.
reputation.noRatings: No ratings yet: they come in with your first passengers.
reputation.note: Last week's passengers: points compared with what they expect of the class. Seat = seat product and pitch; aircraft = age (new is nicer); price = value for money; crowding = very full cabins; cancellations = passengers whose flight was cancelled. Punctuality and service join in Phase 9.

away.title: While you were away
away.catchingUp: Catching up the time you were away: {{from}} → {{to}} …
away.note: Your flights kept flying and the other airlines kept reacting. Nobody made decisions for you — managers who can come in Phase 8.

cloud.title: Cloud sync
cloud.unavailable: Cloud sync isn't set up in this version yet.
cloud.intro: Sign in with your Google account to keep your games the same on phone and computer. Your saves are stored in the game's free Firebase database; only you can read them.
cloud.auto: Syncs automatically: when the app starts, when you leave it, when you come back and every few minutes while you play.
cloud.failed: Sync didn't work ({{error}}). Your saves on this device are safe; it tries again later.
cloud.conflict: {{name}} was played on this device and on another one: here {{here}}, in the cloud {{there}}. Which one do you want to continue? The other one is kept as a copy.

maint.intro: Aircraft need checks to stay airworthy. A-checks (every few hundred flight hours) are done overnight at your hub if the aircraft spends a long enough night there; otherwise it loses a day. C-checks (every 2–3 years) and D-checks (heavy structural checks every 10–12 years, including a C-check) take it out of service for days or weeks: its flights are cancelled. The game plans each heavy check about 4 months ahead, in the low season when it can; you can move it.
maint.reservesValue: {{amount}} with the lessor ({{rate}} per flight hour)
maint.moveAsk: {{check}} from {{date}}: {{days}} days in the hangar, {{price}} at {{where}}. The aircraft's flights are cancelled while it is in the hangar.
maint.shortNotice: Less than 30 days' notice: the MRO charges 25 % extra.
maint.fromReserves: The lessor pays {{amount}} of it from the reserves.
maint.hangarIntro: Most young airlines pay a maintenance company (MRO) per check. Your own hangar at the hub makes every check about 45 % cheaper and always has a bay free, but it costs a lot to build and to run (mechanics, tools, energy): it pays off with a big fleet.

sizeHint.narrow: 2 bays for turboprops, regional and narrow-body jets
sizeHint.wide: 2 bays for any aircraft, wide-bodies included

maint.hangarFacts: Building {{price}} (30 % now, the rest when it is ready in 18 months); running costs {{running}} a day.
maint.buildAsk: Build a {{size}} at {{airport}} for {{price}}? {{now}} is paid now, the rest when it is ready on {{date}}.
maint.costNote: Costs: A-checks are an expense of the day; C- and D-checks are written off until the same check is due again. Leased aircraft pay reserves to the lessor every flight hour, and the lessor pays the heavy checks from them. Technical failures happen more often on old aircraft and close to a check: flights are cancelled, passengers get compensation (EU 261) and rate you badly.

livery.title: Livery designer
livery.intro: Design how your aircraft look: colours, patterns for the fuselage and the tail, a logo, the titles and your own drawing on top. New aircraft arrive in the new livery; the ones already flying keep the old one until they are repainted.
livery.saveHint_one: Saving makes this your livery for new aircraft. Your {{count}} aircraft in service keeps the old one until it is repainted.
livery.saveHint_other: Saving makes this your livery for new aircraft. Your {{count}} aircraft in service keep the old one until they are repainted.
livery.oldFleet_one: {{count}} aircraft still wears an older livery. Repainting costs about {{price}} and {{days}} days in the paint hangar, or no extra days together with its next C- or D-check.
livery.oldFleet_other: {{count}} aircraft still wear an older livery. Repainting costs about {{price}} each and {{days}} days in the paint hangar, or no extra days together with their next C- or D-check.
livery.allWithCheck: Repaint all with their next check
livery.allAtCheck_one: {{count}} aircraft will be repainted during its next C- or D-check.
livery.allAtCheck_other: {{count}} aircraft will be repainted during their next C- or D-check.
livery.uploadNote: Only use a picture you made yourself or are allowed to use (no real airline logos). It is shrunk to a small square so saves stay small.
livery.imageLoaded: Your picture is on the tail. Upload another one to replace it.
livery.titlesOn: Show the airline name on the fuselage
livery.drawIntro: Draw your own lines and shapes on the aircraft: switch drawing on, then draw on the preview with the mouse or your finger. Everything outside the aircraft is cut off. Drawings stretch with the aircraft shape.
livery.repaintPlanned: Repaint planned with the next C- or D-check.
livery.repaintAsk: Repaint now for {{price}}? The aircraft is out of service for {{days}} days; its flights are cancelled meanwhile.

types.title: Aircraft encyclopedia
types.intro: Every aircraft type in the game, from the DC-3 to the newest jets: when it was built and flown, its specs and its price. Historical types become flyable with historical start years (Phase 5); types still flying today can show up on the lease and used markets.
types.legend: Timeline 1930–2035: thick cyan bar = years it was built; thin line = years in passenger service (green while still flying, grey once retired); magenta = your game's year.
types.etopsMulti: three or four engines: no limit
types.etopsMin: up to {{min}} minutes from an airport
types.priceNote: List prices are in the money of their time, converted with the US consumer price index (BLS, public domain). Airlines usually paid much less after discounts.
types.orderable: Can be ordered new from the factory (Fleet → Order new).
types.marketOnly: No longer built, but still flying: used aircraft can show up on the lease and used markets.
types.freighterLater: A freighter: cargo flights come in a later phase.
types.historical: Not built or flown in your game's year. Start a game in the years it flew (New game → start year) to lease or buy it.
types.source: Specs are rounded manufacturer and encyclopedic figures, typed in by hand; retirement years are approximate.

world.title: World situation
world.fuelHint: Spot price, last 52 weeks. Real prices until 23 Oct 2026, then simulated: it swings like the real market and drifts back to its long-run level; fuel shocks push it up. Fares follow fuel a little.
world.fxHint: Rate of {{date}}. Leases and fuel are paid in dollars, your books are in your own currency: exchange rates change your costs.
world.demandHint: Recessions hit business travel hardest; pandemics hit international travel hardest.
world.growthHint: Air travel grows about 3 % a year in the long run; your competitors grow their capacity with it.
world.realPeriod: Until {{date}} the game follows the real world: real fuel prices, exchange rates and real events (see History); only small things like storms and short strikes are added at random. After that the world is simulated.
world.openClosureLine: {{share}} % of flights cancelled · no end in sight
world.trafficTodayHint: How many people flew then, compared with 2024 (from each country's population and wealth, calibrated on the World Bank's passenger figures). Markets and your competitors' flights are this much smaller.

history.title: World history
history.intro: The real world since 1970 as the game knows it: jet fuel prices, exchange rates, air travel and the real events that shook the airlines. Games that start in the past (coming in step 5.3) live through all of it; until the real data ends in October 2026 these events also happen in today's games.
history.chartHint: Line chart from {{from}} to {{to}}. Move over it to read single values.
history.fuelLabel: Jet fuel price per US gallon since 1970
history.fuelNote: US EIA: Gulf Coast spot price from April 1990; before that the refiners' wholesale price (from July 1975, scaled to the spot level) and, until mid-1975, estimated from crude oil prices. "In 2025 dollars" removes inflation (US consumer prices).
history.fxLegacy: {{currency}} was replaced by the euro on {{date}} at {{rate}} per euro; after that its line follows the euro.
history.fxNote: Monthly averages of the Federal Reserve's daily rates where it publishes the currency, otherwise World Bank yearly averages. Currencies that were later re-based (Turkish lira, Polish złoty, Brazilian real …) are shown in today's units.
history.trafficLabel: Passengers carried by the world's airlines per year since 1970
history.trafficNote: The game's demand follows each country's population and wealth (World Bank) plus the long-term trend to cheaper flying. Dips such as 1991, 2001, 2009 and 2020 come from the events below. Jumps in the real line (e.g. 2010) are changes in how the statistics were counted.
history.timelineNote: Strengths are estimates (modelled). Each event links to the Wikipedia article its facts come from. Events still going on in October 2026 end at a different, unknown date in every game.
history.effectFuel: shown in the real fuel price

jumbo1970.name: The jumbo jet enters service
jumbo1970.text: Pan Am flies the first Boeing 747 from New York to London: twice as many seats, much lower cost per seat.

brettonWoods1971.name: End of fixed exchange rates
brettonWoods1971.text: The US ends the dollar's convertibility into gold; within two years the major currencies float freely.

yomKippur1973.name: Yom Kippur War
yomKippur1973.text: War between Israel, Egypt and Syria closes the airspace of the three countries.

oil1973.name: First oil crisis
oil1973.text: The Arab oil embargo quadruples the oil price; jet fuel goes from about 12 to over 30 US cents a gallon.

recession1974.name: Recession after the oil crisis
recession1974.text: The world economy shrinks; airlines cut flights and fares rise.

concorde1976.name: Concorde enters service
concorde1976.text: British Airways and Air France start supersonic flights.

skytrain1977.name: Laker Skytrain
skytrain1977.text: Laker Airways sells walk-on London–New York tickets at a fraction of the usual fare, an early low-cost airline.

blizzard1978.name: Blizzard of 1978
blizzard1978.text: A huge snowstorm shuts the airports of New England and New York for days.

deregulation1978.name: US airline deregulation
deregulation1978.text: The Airline Deregulation Act lets US airlines choose routes and fares freely: competition, new airlines and lower fares.

oil1979.name: Second oil crisis
oil1979.text: The Iranian revolution doubles the oil price; jet fuel nearly triples within two years.

recession1980.name: Early 1980s recession
recession1980.text: High interest rates against inflation push North America and Europe into recession.

stHelens1980.name: Mount St. Helens
stHelens1980.text: The eruption covers eastern Washington in ash; Spokane and Yakima airports close.

iranIraq1980.name: Iran–Iraq War
iranIraq1980.text: Eight years of war restrict flying in both countries.

patco1981.name: US air traffic controllers' strike
patco1981.text: Over 11,000 striking controllers are fired; the FAA cuts flights at the big airports by about a quarter.

patcoRebuild1981.name: Rebuilding US air traffic control
patcoRebuild1981.text: Flow restrictions stay while new controllers are trained.

falklands1982.name: Falklands War
falklands1982.text: Flights to the Falkland Islands stop during the war.

debtCrisis1982.name: Latin American debt crisis
debtCrisis1982.text: Mexico cannot pay its debts; Mexico, Brazil and Argentina fall into a long crisis.

fear1986.name: Americans stay away from Europe
fear1986.text: After terror attacks and the bombing of Libya many US travellers cancel trips to Europe.

chernobyl1986.name: Chernobyl disaster
chernobyl1986.text: The nuclear accident frightens travellers in Eastern and Central Europe.

eu1987.name: First EU aviation package
eu1987.text: Europe starts to open its air transport market: more freedom on fares and capacity.

tiananmen1989.name: Tiananmen Square
tiananmen1989.text: After the crackdown in Beijing, tourism to China collapses for months.

redoubt1989.name: Redoubt eruption
redoubt1989.text: Ash from Mount Redoubt closes Anchorage airport.

wall1989.name: Fall of the Berlin Wall
wall1989.text: The Iron Curtain opens: Vienna becomes the gateway to Eastern Europe.

gulf1990.name: Gulf crisis oil shock
gulf1990.text: Iraq invades Kuwait; the jet fuel price more than doubles within two months.

kuwait1990.name: Invasion of Kuwait
kuwait1990.text: Kuwait's airport is closed until after its liberation.

iraqSanctions1990.name: Sanctions against Iraq
iraqSanctions1990.text: UN sanctions stop international flights to Iraq for over a decade.

recession1990.name: Early 1990s recession
recession1990.text: The US, the UK and other countries fall into recession.

gulfWar1991.name: Gulf War
gulfWar1991.text: Fear of terrorism: international air travel drops sharply worldwide during the war.

yugoslavia1991.name: Wars in Yugoslavia
yugoslavia1991.text: War closes most airports in Croatia, Bosnia and Serbia.

bosnia1992.name: Siege of Sarajevo
bosnia1992.text: Sarajevo has no civil flights until 1996, only the humanitarian airlift.

pinatubo1991.name: Pinatubo eruption
pinatubo1991.text: One of the largest eruptions of the century closes Manila and Clark airports.

panAm1991.name: Pan Am stops flying
panAm1991.text: The most famous US airline goes out of business after 64 years.

ussr1991.name: End of the Soviet Union
ussr1991.text: Fifteen new countries; Aeroflot is split into many airlines.

andrew1992.name: Hurricane Andrew
andrew1992.text: Andrew devastates South Florida; Miami's airports close.

spurr1992.name: Spurr eruption
spurr1992.text: Ash from Mount Spurr closes Anchorage airport.

blackWednesday1992.name: Black Wednesday
blackWednesday1992.text: The pound and the lira leave the European exchange rate mechanism.

eu1993.name: EU single aviation market
eu1993.text: Any EU airline may fly between EU countries and set its own fares.

tequila1994.name: Mexican peso crisis
tequila1994.text: The peso loses half its value; Mexico falls into a deep recession.

austriaEu1995.name: Austria joins the EU
austriaEu1995.text: Austria, Finland and Sweden become EU members.

schengen1995.name: Schengen area
schengen1995.text: Passport checks between the first Schengen countries end.

cabotage1997.name: Full EU cabotage
cabotage1997.text: EU airlines may also fly domestic routes in other EU countries.

asia1997.name: Asian financial crisis
asia1997.text: Currencies of Thailand, Indonesia, Korea and others crash; travel from Asia falls.

chekLapKok1998.name: New Hong Kong airport
chekLapKok1998.text: Chek Lap Kok replaces Kai Tak and its famous approach over the city.

russia1998.name: Russian financial crisis
russia1998.text: The rouble collapses and Russia defaults.

euro1999.name: The euro is born
euro1999.text: Eleven countries fix their exchange rates: 1 euro = 13.7603 Austrian schillings.

kosovo1999.name: Kosovo War
kosovo1999.text: NATO air strikes close the airspace of Yugoslavia for 11 weeks.

starAlliance2000.name: Austrian joins Star Alliance
starAlliance2000.text: The Austrian Airlines Group becomes a Star Alliance member.

dotcom2001.name: Dot-com recession
dotcom2001.text: The internet bubble bursts; business travel in the US drops.

turkey2001.name: Turkish financial crisis
turkey2001.text: The lira loses half its value.

sept11Closure.name: September 11
sept11Closure.text: After the attacks in the US, the airspace of the US and Canada is closed for days.

sept11.name: Fear of flying after 9/11
sept11.text: US air travel falls by about a fifth; airlines go bankrupt or need help.

sept11World.name: Worldwide drop after 9/11
sept11World.text: Air travel falls worldwide, especially long-haul.

swissair2001.name: Swissair grounding
swissair2001.text: Swissair runs out of money; its whole fleet stays on the ground.

sabena2001.name: Sabena bankrupt
sabena2001.text: Belgium's national airline goes out of business.

argentina2001.name: Argentine crisis
argentina2001.text: Argentina defaults and the peso is devalued.

euroCash2002.name: Euro notes and coins
euroCash2002.text: Euro cash replaces the schilling and the other old currencies.

bali2002.name: Bali bombings
bali2002.text: Terror attacks on tourists keep visitors away from Indonesia.

iraq2003.name: Iraq War
iraq2003.text: The invasion of Iraq makes people avoid international travel for some weeks.

sars2003.name: SARS
sars2003.text: The new lung disease almost empties flights to Hong Kong, China and Singapore.

sarsAsia2003.name: SARS in Asia
sarsAsia2003.text: Travel throughout Asia falls during the outbreak.

concordeEnd2003.name: Concorde's last flight
concordeEnd2003.text: British Airways and Air France retire the Concorde.

tsunami2004.name: Indian Ocean tsunami
tsunami2004.text: The tsunami devastates coasts; tourists stay away from Thailand, Sri Lanka and the Maldives.

katrina2005.name: Hurricane Katrina
katrina2005.text: New Orleans is flooded; its airport has no airline flights for two weeks.

liquids2006.name: Liquids plot
liquids2006.text: A foiled bomb plot brings strict security and mass cancellations at London's airports; liquid limits follow.

a380_2007.name: First A380 flight
a380_2007.text: Singapore Airlines flies the first Airbus A380 from Singapore to Sydney.

openSkies2008.name: EU–US Open Skies
openSkies2008.text: Any EU or US airline may fly between any EU and US cities.

fuel2008.name: Oil price record
fuel2008.text: Oil reaches 147 dollars a barrel; jet fuel almost 4 dollars a gallon.

recession2008.name: Global financial crisis
recession2008.text: After Lehman Brothers collapses the world falls into recession; business travel drops sharply.

iceland2008.name: Icelandic banking collapse
iceland2008.text: Iceland's banks fail and the króna crashes.

bangkok2008.name: Bangkok airports occupied
bangkok2008.text: Protesters occupy both Bangkok airports for over a week.

h1n1_2009.name: Swine flu
h1n1_2009.text: The new flu starts in Mexico; travel to Mexico collapses for weeks.

austrianLufthansa2009.name: Lufthansa takes over Austrian
austrianLufthansa2009.text: Austrian Airlines becomes part of the Lufthansa Group.

eyjafjallajokull2010.name: Eyjafjallajökull ash cloud
eyjafjallajokull2010.text: The ash cloud from Iceland closes most of European airspace for six days: about 100,000 flights cancelled.

euroCrisis2010.name: European debt crisis
euroCrisis2010.text: Greece, Portugal, Ireland, Spain, Italy and Cyprus fall into a long crisis.

merapi2010.name: Merapi eruption
merapi2010.text: Ash closes Yogyakarta and Solo airports.

spainAtc2010.name: Spanish controllers' walkout
spainAtc2010.text: Air traffic controllers walk out; Spain's airspace is closed for a day and a half.

snow2010.name: December 2010 snow
snow2010.text: Heavy snow paralyses Heathrow for days just before Christmas, and other big airports too.

arabSpring2011.name: Arab Spring
arabSpring2011.text: Revolutions in Egypt and Tunisia; tourists stay away.

libya2011.name: Libyan civil war
libya2011.text: A no-fly zone closes Libyan airspace.

tohoku2011.name: Japan earthquake and tsunami
tohoku2011.text: The earthquake and the Fukushima disaster keep visitors away from Japan.

sendai2011.name: Sendai airport flooded
sendai2011.text: The tsunami floods Sendai airport; it reopens a month later.

grimsvotn2011.name: Grímsvötn ash
grimsvotn2011.text: Ash closes Iceland and Scottish airports for a few days.

puyehue2011.name: Puyehue ash
puyehue2011.text: Ash from Chile closes Buenos Aires and Bariloche airports again and again.

puyehueOceania2011.name: Puyehue ash over Australia
puyehueOceania2011.text: The ash cloud circles the globe and grounds flights in Australia and New Zealand.

bangkokFlood2011.name: Bangkok floods
bangkokFlood2011.text: Don Mueang airport is flooded for months.

ets2012.name: Aviation joins the EU ETS
ets2012.text: Airlines must buy CO2 allowances for flights within Europe.

vieCheckIn3_2012.name: Vienna Check-in 3
vieCheckIn3_2012.text: Vienna airport opens its new terminal (Skylink), now Terminal 3.

syria2012.name: Syrian civil war
syria2012.text: Western airlines stop flying to Syria and avoid its airspace.

sandy2012.name: Hurricane Sandy
sandy2012.text: New York's airports close for days.

egypt2013.name: Unrest in Egypt
egypt2013.text: After the coup many countries warn against travel to Egypt.

kelud2014.name: Kelud eruption
kelud2014.text: Ash closes seven airports on Java.

donbas2014.name: War in eastern Ukraine
donbas2014.text: Donetsk and Luhansk airports are destroyed in the fighting.

libya2014.name: Second Libyan civil war
libya2014.text: Tripoli airport is destroyed; only a few airlines still fly to Libya.

ebola2014.name: Ebola in West Africa
ebola2014.text: Airlines stop flying to Liberia, Sierra Leone and Guinea.

russia2014.name: Rouble crisis
russia2014.text: Sanctions and the oil price fall halve the rouble; Russians travel much less abroad.

yemen2015.name: War in Yemen
yemen2015.text: Yemen's airspace is closed to normal air traffic.

mers2015.name: MERS in South Korea
mers2015.text: An outbreak keeps visitors away from Korea.

sousse2015.name: Sousse attack
sousse2015.text: After the attack on a beach hotel the UK advises against travel to Tunisia for two years.

raung2015.name: Raung ash
raung2015.text: Ash closes Bali airport for days.

sinaiUk2015.name: UK flights to Sharm el-Sheikh stopped
sinaiUk2015.text: After a bomb downs a Russian airliner, the UK suspends flights to Sharm el-Sheikh for four years.

sinaiRussia2015.name: Russian flights to Egypt's resorts stopped
sinaiRussia2015.text: Russia suspends flights to Sharm el-Sheikh and Hurghada until 2021.

cairoRussia2015.name: Russian flights to Cairo stopped
cairoRussia2015.text: Flights between Russia and Cairo resume in 2018.

paris2015.name: Paris attacks
paris2015.text: Terror attacks in Paris make some travellers avoid France.

blizzard2016.name: Blizzard of 2016
blizzard2016.text: A blizzard closes the airports from Washington to New York.

turkey2016.name: Turkey's difficult year
turkey2016.text: Attacks and a coup attempt; tourism to Turkey falls by about a third.

brussels2016.name: Brussels airport attack
brussels2016.text: After the bombing in the departure hall the airport stays closed for 12 days.

qatarBlockade2017.name: Qatar blockade
qatarBlockade2017.text: Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain and Egypt cut all flights to Qatar until 2021.

irmaSxm2017.name: Irma destroys St. Maarten airport
irmaSxm2017.text: Hurricane Irma wrecks Princess Juliana airport; it reopens a month later.

irma2017.name: Hurricane Irma in Florida
irma2017.text: Florida's airports close as Irma passes.

maria2017.name: Hurricane Maria
maria2017.text: Puerto Rico is devastated; San Juan airport works with few flights for weeks.

airBerlin2017.name: Air Berlin's last flight
airBerlin2017.text: Germany's second-largest airline stops flying after insolvency.

agung2017.name: Agung eruption
agung2017.text: Ash closes Bali and Lombok airports for three days.

niki2017.name: NIKI insolvent
niki2017.text: Air Berlin's Austrian subsidiary NIKI files for insolvency; Niki Lauda buys it back as Laudamotion.

beastFromTheEast2018.name: Beast from the East
beastFromTheEast2018.text: A cold wave with heavy snow closes Dublin and Scottish airports.

turkey2018.name: Turkish currency crisis
turkey2018.text: The lira crashes; Turks travel less abroad.

jebi2018.name: Typhoon Jebi
jebi2018.text: Kansai airport is flooded and cut off from the mainland.

mangkhut2018.name: Typhoon Mangkhut
mangkhut2018.text: Hong Kong and Macau airports stop flights.

gatwickDrone2018.name: Gatwick drones
gatwickDrone2018.text: Drone sightings close Gatwick for 33 hours before Christmas.

pakistan2019.name: Pakistan closes its airspace
pakistan2019.text: After clashes with India, Pakistan's airspace is closed for months.

max2019.name: 737 MAX grounded
max2019.text: After two crashes the Boeing 737 MAX is grounded worldwide until late 2020.

istanbul2019.name: Istanbul's new airport
istanbul2019.text: Overnight, Atatürk airport's flights move to the new Istanbul Airport.

hongKong2019.name: Hong Kong airport protests
hongKong2019.text: Protests in the terminal stop departures for two days.

hongKongProtests2019.name: Hong Kong protests
hongKongProtests2019.text: Months of protests keep visitors away.

thomasCook2019.name: Thomas Cook collapses
thomasCook2019.text: The world's oldest travel company goes bust; 150,000 holidaymakers are flown home.

hagibis2019.name: Typhoon Hagibis
hagibis2019.text: Tokyo's airports cancel almost all flights.

covidChina2020.name: COVID-19 in China
covidChina2020.text: Wuhan is locked down; China closes its borders almost completely until 2023.

covid2020.name: COVID-19 pandemic
covid2020.text: Borders close worldwide; in April 2020 air travel falls by over 90 %. Recovery takes three years.

ber2020.name: Berlin Brandenburg opens
ber2020.text: Nine years late, Berlin's new airport opens.

belarus2021.name: EU bans flights to Belarus
belarus2021.text: After Belarus forces down a Ryanair jet, the EU bans flights between the EU and Belarus.

afghanistan2021.name: Fall of Kabul
afghanistan2021.text: After the Taliban take power only a few airlines still fly to Afghanistan.

ita2021.name: ITA replaces Alitalia
ita2021.text: Alitalia stops flying; ITA Airways takes over.

ukraine2022.name: Russian invasion of Ukraine
ukraine2022.text: Ukraine's airspace is closed to civil flights; Moldova's too at first.

russiaBan2022.name: No flights between Russia and the West
russiaBan2022.text: The EU, UK, US, Canada and others close their airspace to Russian airlines; Russia does the same.

fuel2022.name: Energy crisis 2022
fuel2022.text: The war drives jet fuel to record prices.

sudan2023.name: War in Sudan
sudan2023.text: Fighting closes Khartoum airport and Sudan's airspace.

natsFailure2023.name: UK air traffic control failure
natsFailure2023.text: A software fault at NATS cancels over 1,500 flights in one day.

israel2023.name: Gaza war
israel2023.text: Most foreign airlines stop flying to Tel Aviv for months.

iranIsrael2024.name: Iranian strikes on Israel
iranIsrael2024.text: Israel, Jordan, Iraq, Iran and Lebanon close their airspace overnight.

heathrowFire2025.name: Heathrow power cut
heathrowFire2025.text: A fire at an electrical substation closes Heathrow for a day.

twelveDayWar2025.name: Twelve-Day War
twelveDayWar2025.text: War between Israel and Iran closes the airspace of Iran, Iraq, Israel and Jordan.

gulf2025.name: Gulf airspace closed
gulf2025.text: After Iran's strike on a US base, Qatar, Bahrain and Kuwait close their airspace for hours.

bulgariaEuro2026.name: Bulgaria adopts the euro
bulgariaEuro2026.text: The lev is replaced at 1.95583 per euro.

iranWar2026.name: Iran war
iranWar2026.text: US and Israeli strikes on Iran and Iranian attacks on Gulf states close airspace around the Gulf until the ceasefire of 8 April.

iranWarIran2026.name: Iran's airspace closed
iranWarIran2026.text: Flights to Iran resume step by step from July 2026.

iranWarQatar2026.name: Qatar's airspace closed
iranWarQatar2026.text: Qatar closes its airspace; from 7 March only Qatar Airways flies, foreign airlines return from 21 April.

iranWarGulf2026.name: Gulf flights disrupted
iranWarGulf2026.text: Missile and drone attacks disrupt many flights in the Emirates, Oman and Saudi Arabia (share of cancellations estimated).

iranWarFuel2026.name: Iran war oil shock
iranWarFuel2026.text: Jet fuel nearly doubles within weeks and stays high.

iranWarDemand2026.name: Travellers avoid the Middle East
iranWarDemand2026.text: Demand for travel to the Gulf region falls sharply (estimated).
